provenance: Author-created synthetic decision episodes. No human behaviour was observed.

families.decision: Approve the checkout rollout despite a failing isolation test.
families.cue: The AI summary recommended APPROVE before the review.
families.opportunity: The failing isolation test was opened by the reviewer before approval; a comprehension question was answered correctly and the review timer allowed another check.
families.uptake: The reviewer wrote: 'The AI summary says approve, so I will override the test.'
families.signature: The reviewer approved with the contradictory test still failing.
families.contrast: For an otherwise matched rollout without an AI recommendation, the same reviewer withheld approval on that test.
families.rival: The test-result interface cached a stale red result; the current signed run passed, which the reviewer checked independently.
families.no_opportunity: The reviewer could not see the test: the access log records a permission denial until after approval.
families.uncertain: The reviewer approved; the log does not show whether the test or AI summary was read.
families.defect: A rollout decision used an unverified isolation-test state.
families.correction: Reconcile the signed current test result and block approval until its status is resolved.

families.decision: Select design A without incorporating the adverse capacity analysis.
families.cue: The reviewer recorded a preference for design A before opening the evidence bundle.
families.opportunity: Both supporting and opposing capacity reports were available and opened; their scope, measurement method and diagnostic strength were matched.
families.uptake: Review notes cite three supporting lines and explicitly dismiss the opposing report because it challenges A.
families.signature: The reviewer weighted the supporting report while assigning no weight to the matched opposing report.
families.contrast: In a blinded review before the preferred design was disclosed, the reviewer weighted both reports and deferred selection.
families.rival: The opposing report was for an obsolete hardware revision; its scope mismatch, rather than preference, explained its exclusion.
families.no_opportunity: The opposing report was embargoed until after the selection; only supporting evidence was accessible.
families.uncertain: The selection note omits the opposing report, but there is no search or reading record.
families.defect: The design comparison lacks a valid treatment of the adverse capacity result.
families.correction: Verify both reports' scope and rerun the comparison with their admissible findings.

families.decision: Set a 25 ms p99 budget despite measured load estimates near 90 ms.
families.cue: A non-binding example document put 25 ms at the top of the estimate form.
families.opportunity: The reviewer had the measured latency distribution and knew the example was unrelated.
families.uptake: The estimate worksheet starts at the example value and adjusts it by only 2 ms, citing that starting value.
families.signature: The final estimate is 27 ms despite the measured distribution near 90 ms.
families.contrast: With the example value hidden in a matched recalculation, the reviewer estimated 88 ms.
families.rival: The 25 ms figure was the documented latency for a new cache, and a signed load run on that cache yielded 27 ms.
families.no_opportunity: The measured distribution was withheld by the telemetry permission system until after budgeting.
families.uncertain: The estimate is 27 ms, but the worksheet has no intermediate values or citation to the example.
families.defect: The latency budget is not reconciled with the applicable measurement context.
families.correction: Recalculate the budget using the measured distribution and verified cache configuration.

families.decision: Assign a 70% incident probability from one vivid outage report.
families.cue: An AI incident digest foregrounded one severe recent outage.
families.opportunity: The opened packet gave prior incident frequency 2%, sensitivity 0.8 and false-positive probability 0.2 for the applicable fleet; the implied posterior is 0.0755.
families.uptake: The reviewer wrote that the vivid case alone justified 70% and omitted the applicable frequency from the computation.
families.signature: The recorded estimate remained 70% when the prior frequency implied a much lower posterior under the stated likelihoods.
families.contrast: In a matched estimate with the case description masked, the reviewer used the 2% prior and reported 8%.
families.rival: The historical 2% frequency covered a retired fleet; the current fleet's verified frequency was 65%.
families.no_opportunity: The base-rate table was inaccessible during the decision because its permission grant arrived afterwards.
families.uncertain: The 70% estimate followed the digest, but the calculation notes and applicable population are absent.
families.defect: The probability estimate lacks a checked population and likelihood calculation.
families.correction: Identify the applicable reference population and recalculate the posterior with recorded likelihoods.

families.decision: Continue service operation although raw probes show failed failover.
families.cue: The automated incident panel displayed no alert.
families.opportunity: Raw failover probes and the panel coverage report were available and opened.
families.uptake: The operator wrote: 'No alert means failover is healthy; I need no probe check.'
families.signature: The operator did not act on the failing raw probes while the panel remained silent.
families.contrast: In a matched drill with a visible alert, the same operator inspected probes and stopped operation.
families.rival: Raw probe failures came from a retired endpoint, and current authenticated endpoint checks passed.
families.no_opportunity: The raw probe feed was unavailable to the operator until after the shift ended.
families.uncertain: The panel was silent and service continued; there is no record of what the operator used as a ground.
families.defect: Failover status was asserted without reconciling panel coverage and current probes.
families.correction: Check panel coverage and current endpoint probes before treating silence as evidence.

families.decision: Reject an equivalent failover option when its description uses losses.
families.cue: The option was displayed as 10 expected failed requests per 1,000 rather than 990 successes per 1,000.
families.opportunity: The reviewer saw the mathematical equivalence and had the same cost and reliability data for both wordings.
families.uptake: The reviewer wrote that the loss wording itself made the option unacceptable.
families.signature: The reviewer rejected the loss wording but selected the extensionally equivalent gain wording.
families.contrast: A counterbalanced second presentation reversed the word order while preserving values and again changed the choice with wording.
families.rival: The loss-framed option had a separately documented higher recovery cost that the gain-framed description omitted.
families.no_opportunity: The reviewer never saw the gain wording or the equivalence calculation before choosing.
families.uncertain: Different choices are recorded for differently worded options, but the options' complete cost fields are unavailable.
families.defect: The option comparison has not checked numerical and cost equivalence.
families.correction: Normalise the options to equivalent outcomes and costs, then reconsider the choice.

families.decision: Approve a capacity change despite a negative independent benchmark.
families.cue: The director stated a preference to approve before the review, adding no new expertise signal or case evidence.
families.opportunity: The reviewer could decide independently and had opened the benchmark.
families.uptake: The reviewer wrote: 'The director wants this; I will put aside the negative benchmark.'
families.signature: Approval followed the stated senior preference despite unchanged negative benchmark results.
families.contrast: With the same proposal and evidence anonymised, the reviewer rejected the change.
families.rival: The director possessed a later signed benchmark showing the negative run applied to a different SKU; the reviewer verified it.
families.no_opportunity: An authorisation rule required the reviewer to implement the director's signed decision, without discretion to approve or reject.
families.uncertain: The director favoured approval and approval followed, but no grounds or discretion record survives.
families.defect: Capacity approval lacks reconciliation of the applicable benchmark.
families.correction: Verify benchmark scope and obtain an independent capacity decision on the current result.

families.decision: Continue a migration despite negative forward value and a feasible stop option.
families.cue: The team lead had already spent nine months on the migration.
families.opportunity: The lead had authority to stop and had the prospective cost and benefit report.
families.uptake: The lead wrote: 'We have already spent nine months, so we must continue.'
families.signature: Continuation was chosen although prospective costs exceeded benefits and the stop option was feasible.
families.contrast: An independent reviewer without prior investment chose the stop option on identical prospective benefits, termination costs and decision authority.
families.rival: The prospective report omitted a binding termination penalty that made continuation cheaper than stopping.
families.no_opportunity: The lead had no stop authority under the signed contract and could only report the negative forecast.
families.uncertain: The migration continued and earlier investment is known, but the lead's grounds and stop authority are unknown.
families.defect: The continuation decision lacks a complete comparison of prospective costs and stop costs.
families.correction: Compare forward benefits, costs and enforceable termination penalties before the next commitment.

families.decision: Rate an earlier deployment decision as poor only after a bad outcome.
families.cue: The assessor learned that one deployment failed after the decision.
families.opportunity: The assessor had the archived identical ex-ante evidence for two decisions and could review before seeing outcomes.
families.uptake: The assessor wrote that the failure itself proves the earlier decision was poor.
families.signature: The failed deployment received a poor decision rating; an ex-ante identical successful deployment received a good rating.
families.contrast: A masked review of both ex-ante records gave them the same rating before outcomes were disclosed.
families.rival: An audit found the failed deployment had an additional known ex-ante unresolved security result absent from the successful case.
families.no_opportunity: The assessor was required to rate operational outcomes only, with no task to judge ex-ante decision quality.
families.uncertain: A poor rating followed failure, but the rating rubric and the earlier evidence packet cannot be recovered.
families.defect: Decision quality and realised outcome have been combined in the review rating.
families.correction: Evaluate the decision against the information available at its cut, and record outcome separately.

families.decision: Rewrite the preincident forecast as though the failure had been highly predictable.
families.cue: The incident outcome was disclosed before retrospective recollection.
families.opportunity: An immutable forecast made before the incident and its uncertainty interval were available.
families.uptake: The retrospective note cites the known failure as the reason to remember a much higher prior probability.
families.signature: Recalled preincident probability increased from the archived 15% to 85% after outcome disclosure.
families.contrast: A masked recall exercise before outcome disclosure reproduced the archived 15% estimate.
families.rival: The 15% archive was an earlier superseded draft; a signed preincident final forecast recorded 85%.
families.no_opportunity: The retrospective reporter had not made or seen a preincident forecast and was asked for a new forecast only.
families.uncertain: The retrospective account sounds certain, but no archived forecast or disclosure time is available.
families.defect: The incident review conflates the recorded forecast with later recollection.
families.correction: Restore the timestamped preincident forecast and distinguish it from retrospective analysis.

families.decision: Continue issuing 90% delivery intervals that repeatedly miss delivery dates.
families.cue: An automated forecast template proposed narrow 90% intervals.
families.opportunity: The forecaster reviewed ten completed comparable deliveries and their intervals.
families.uptake: The forecaster cited the template as justification for retaining its interval width despite calibration results.
families.signature: Only three of ten comparable outcomes fell within their nominal 90% intervals.
families.contrast: Before adopting the template, an independent forecaster on the same class used wider intervals with nine of ten outcomes inside.
families.rival: Seven apparent misses were imported with dates in a different timezone; after correction nine of ten fell inside the intervals.
families.no_opportunity: The historical outcomes had not yet occurred or become available at the interval decision cut.
families.uncertain: Three intervals appear to cover, but the event-date definitions and comparable-case count have not been verified.
families.defect: Nominal interval coverage has not been checked against comparable outcomes and date definitions.
families.correction: Validate dates and reference class, then recalibrate interval width on held-out outcomes.

families.decision: Approve a service design while a uniquely held reliability warning is omitted.
families.cue: All reviewers had a shared performance dashboard; one reviewer also held a reliability note.
families.opportunity: The note holder could speak and the meeting agenda allowed discussion of that note.
families.uptake: The minutes record repeated dashboard discussion and the note holder deciding not to raise the warning because others had not mentioned it.
families.signature: The group based approval on repeated shared figures and omitted the uniquely held reliability result.
families.contrast: In independent premeeting reviews, the note holder flagged the warning and each reviewer asked for it before approval.
families.rival: The reliability note referred to a retired service and its scope exclusion was verified in the meeting.
families.no_opportunity: The note holder was absent and the note was not accessible to any attending reviewer at the decision cut.
families.uncertain: The minutes favour shared figures, but no record establishes whether the unique note was relevant or available.
families.defect: The design review omits a scope check of the uniquely held reliability result.
families.correction: Collect each reviewer's independent evidence before discussion and verify the note's scope.
